title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation
summary: Existing 3D generative approaches are typically developed for individual imaging modalities, requiring substantial modality-specific data and limiting their ability to exploit shared structure across scientific imaging domains. We present SciFusion, a multimodal framework for unified 3D scientific image generation built on a latent diffusion backbone, with two key contributions. First, we introduce a compositional conditioning scheme that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations. Sharing these factors across related modalities enables knowledge transfer across heterogeneous imaging domains and allows the factors to be recombined at inference time to synthesize unseen domain-object-contrast compositions in a zero-shot manner. Second, we incorporate domain-specific physics-informed objectives: Fourier spectral consistency for MRI, Radon projection consistency for CT, and multislice diffraction consistency for electron microscopy, to encourage generated samples to respect modality-dependent image formation processes. Extensive experiments across 15 medical and scientific imaging modalities demonstrate that SciFusion improves generation fidelity and cross-domain generalization over modality-specific and flattened multimodal conditioning strategies, while enabling zero-shot synthesis of unseen compositions without training on those target compositions. These results demonstrate that compositional, physics-guided conditioning provides a scalable framework for unified 3D scientific image generation, particularly for emerging modalities where large-scale training data are difficult to obtain.

title: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Gastric Cancer Detection and Intra-Tumour Progression Analysis
summary: Gastric Cancer is among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The complexity and variability of histopathological images pose significant challenges for both pathologists and computer-based diagnostics, creating a growing need for machine learning approaches capable of capturing meaningful representations from limited labelled data. Selfsupervised Contrastive Learning (CL) has demonstrated promising results in natural image analysis; however, its application to gastric cancer histopathology remains underexplored. This paper proposes an integrated CL framework built on a ResNet50 encoder trained under the NT-Xent objective, without reliance on ImageNet pre-training, to learn discriminative and staining-invariant representations from H&E-stained tissue patches. The learned embeddings are transferred to a supervised downstream classifier for binary tumour/normal (TUM/NOR) detection, achieving a test accuracy of 83.13%, an AUC-ROC of 0.9087, and an Average Precision of 0.9063 - competitive with recent supervised and weakly-supervised approaches on comparable histopathology benchmarks. Beyond binary diagnosis, the framework applies K-Means clustering to tumour embeddings to identify four geometrically separable pseudo-stage clusters, confirmed by a Random Forest classifier achieving 97% accuracy and a mean Dice coefficient of 0.97, demonstrating the capacity of CL representations to encode progression-relevant morphological variation without stage-level annotations. Grad-CAM explainability is integrated throughout to ensure model transparency. The complete system is deployed via a Streamlit clinical interface. Compared to recent state-of-the-art methods the proposed framework operates with substantially fewer labelled samples while additionally providing unsupervised progression stratification and interpretable outputs, addressing a gap not covered by existing approaches.

title: Unified Projection-Domain Material Decomposition for Energy-Integrating and Photon-Counting CT
summary: Objective: To develop a unified and efficient method for projection-domain material decomposition in spectral computed tomography (CT) that incorporates an arbitrary number of spectral measurements, independent of the acquisition mechanism, without reducing the measurements to two effective energies. Approach: A nested optimization method was developed for two-material basis decomposition from K>=2 spectral measurements. It extends an existing two-measurement univariate method by replacing its polynomial approximation with profile minimization of the Poisson negative log-likelihood, reducing the inversion to two one-dimensional searches that use all measurements without spectral rebinning. The method was evaluated in simulation for energy-integrating (GE Revolution Apex Elite, Siemens SOMATOM Flash) and photon-counting (Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha) CT. Main results: The method recovered line integrals with noiseless iodine errors below 3e-6 g/cm^2 and noise within 3% of the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) agreed, at 70 keV and above, with reference CT numbers and, on all three systems, with vendor VMIs of physical scans (mean absolute error 6-22 HU). For photon counting, four measurements instead of two reduced the iodine CRLB by 19% and image noise by 8-16% at every VMI energy, and lowered the regression error at 70 keV and above. Iteration and tolerance settings changed CT numbers by less than 0.04 HU, and decomposition took 0.34-0.67 s per million rays on an A100 GPU. Significance: The method provides fast, accurate decomposition for any spectral CT acquisition mechanism and number of measurements, so one method can serve every scanner in a virtual imaging trial.

title: Comparing local and global optimization reveals untapped hybrid potentials for machine learning-based inverse planning
summary: Machine learning (ML) models for normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) can be embedded directly into inverse treatment planning, but the resulting optimization problems are generally nonconvex, and the choice between global and local optimization involves a trade-off between optimality guarantees and computational cost. Two open-source frameworks for ML-based inverse planning were compared: OptiCL (global mixed-integer optimization via constraint learning) and pyanno4rt (local nonlinear optimization via end-to-end differentiation). Logistic regression, linear support vector machine, and feed-forward neural network NTCP models for grade 2+ xerostomia and grade 2+ radiation pneumonitis were embedded. Plan optimization was performed for eight head-and-neck (HN) photon cases and seven lung proton cases. The plans were compared by target coverage, OAR dose metrics, spatial dose agreement, post-hoc predicted NTCP, and runtime. A projection-based gradient approximation was introduced to embed decision trees. In addition to that, warm-starting, constraint strengthening, and pruning were investigated as hybrid strategies for combining local and global optimization. Comparing OptiCL and pyanno4rt across the HN and lung treatment plans revealed broadly consistent dose distributions. Mean differences (OptiCL}$-$pyanno4rt [95% CI]) were small: for HN cases, -0.16 Gy [-0.37, 0.06] (parotid) and -0.00 Gy [-0.01, 0.00] (PTV); for lung cases, -0.52 Gy [-1.10, 0.06] (total lung) and -0.04 Gy [-0.07, -0.01] (PTV). Mean NTCP differences amounted to -0.08 p.p. [-0.49, 0.33] (HN) and -1.73 p.p. [-2.68, -0.77] (lung). OptiCL tended toward lower OAR doses and predicted NTCP, but required higher wall-clock runtime. Hybridization of the decision tree-based HN plan eliminated 80% of binary decision variables without compromising plan quality.

title: Equivariant Experience Replay for Continual Learning in Imaging Inverse Problems
summary: In this work, we propose Equivariant Experience Replay, a new paradigm for achieving continual learning of deep networks for solving ill-posed imaging inverse problems. Inspired by recent advances on unsupervised learning methods such as equivariant imaging/splitting, we find the exploitation of group-symmetry structure is particularly relevant and effective in continual learning setting for ill-posed inversion tasks. We therefore propose this new experience replay scheme, which is tailored for such inverse problems. Our numerical study demonstrates the superiority of our method compared to existing continual learning methods for inverse problems in medical imaging and image processing.

title: Advancing oxygen-enhanced MRI acquisition and modelling through dynamic $ΔR_{1}$ and $ΔR_2^*$ sensing
summary:
Purpose: To develop a multiparametric mapping framework for quantifying fat- and water-specific longitudinal and effective transverse relaxation rates, as well as changes in these parameters induced by a gas challenge.
  Theory and Methods: The proposed framework, termed SR-Fat DESPOT (single-reference fat-water separated driven equilibrium single-pulse observation of $T_1$), combines a two-component signal model with a single-reference variable flip angle (SR-VFA) approach. The signal model explicitly incorporates gas challenge-induced changes in relaxation rates. The single-reference acquisition strategy reduces data acquisition requirements while preserving sensitivity to both baseline parameters and dynamic changes. Sequence parameters were optimized using Cramer-Rao lower bound theory. SR-Fat DESPOT was evaluated using a modified open-surce abdominal numerical phantom and in two in vivo experiments: a single participant test-retest experiment and a pilot study with six participants.
  Results: In the abdominal numerical phantom, SR-Fat DESPOT was accurate for quantification of baseline relaxation rates with a normalized median absolute error (nMedAE) <3% for signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) >30 when comparing ground truth and estimates. SR-Fat DESPOT was also able to accurately recover median changes in relaxation rates, with differences within 0.001 $s^-1$ when compared to ground truth. In vivo, SR-Fat DESPOT measured changes in relaxation rates for spleen, kidneys, liver, and muscle under 100% O2 breathing, consistent with reports in literature. Changes detected in the spleen and kidneys were statistically significant across participants.
  Conclusion: SR-Fat DESPOT can quantify changes in relaxation rates induced by a gas challenge while reducing data requirements compared to more conventional approaches used in MR-oximetry literature.

title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
summary: The co-condensation of DNA and proteins plays an important role in genome compaction, including heterochromatin formation and chromosome segregation. Meanwhile, transcription and replication continuously generate DNA supercoiling, yet how the resulting torsional stress affects co-condensation remains poorly understood. Here, by coupling DNA elasticity to a protein concentration field, we show that supercoiling acts as a topological catalyst for co-condensation through a mutually reinforcing interplay with protein wetting. Specifically, protein wetting facilitates twist-to-writhe conversion, generating highly writhed DNA conformations that in turn promote capillary collapse into a protein-rich droplet. In the absence of supercoiling, DNA remains kinetically trapped in metastable extended states within our model, whereas sufficiently strong supercoiling removes the nucleation barrier and enables spontaneous co-condensation. These results establish topology as a distinct control parameter for biomolecular condensation and provide a mechanical framework for how active genomic processes can dynamically regulate large-scale genome organization.

title: Evaporative Cooling and Secondary Combustion in a Liquid-Hydrocarbon Rotating Detonation Combustor with Dual-Purpose Head-End Injection
summary: The rotating detonation engine (RDE) faces severe thermal protection challenges. This study numerically investigates a head-end dual-purpose injection configuration in which the film-cooling holes act as both fuel and coolant injectors. An Eulerian-Lagrangian framework is employed, in which the turbulence closure, the film-cooling effectiveness prediction, and the droplet evaporation model are validated against experimental benchmarks. The validated framework is then applied to examine the effects of coolant flow rate, atomization quality, and the fuel allocation between the main flow and the cooling system. Beyond a threshold coolant flow rate the wall temperature drops substantially, whereas an excessively low flow rate elevates it by intensifying local deflagration, revealing a competition between evaporative cooling and secondary combustion that is inherent to this dual-purpose configuration. Fine droplets cool effectively but only over a limited distance downstream, and fuel allocated to cooling weakens the detonation wave and reduces thrust. A moderate coolant flow rate combined with fine atomization is therefore recommended.

title: CoRE: Relating Fine-Grained Chest X-ray Findings in Anatomical Context
summary: Chest X-ray interpretation depends on both the anatomical location of findings and their relationships with other abnormalities. However, relations defined over global finding labels do not explicitly distinguish the same finding across anatomical locations. We propose CoRE(Co-occurrence-guided Region Evidence), a framework that incorporates relationships among findings and anatomical context into fine-grained chest X-ray prediction. It groups anatomical region-finding labels by co-occurrence and uses these groups to guide shared representation learning through visual prompt tuning on a frozen vision transformer. The predictions are supplemented by an anatomically supervised region-evidence stream through region-matched logit residuals. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR with Chest ImaGenome annotations show that CoRE improves region-finding classification over standard and relation-aware prompt-based baselines. Quantitative evaluations on MS-CXR and the Chest ImaGenome gold standard show improved finding localization, supported by qualitative comparisons. CoRE also improves finding-level classification on mapped finding labels in external VinDr-CXR and CheXpert datasets without target-domain adaptation. These results demonstrate the value of jointly modeling finding relationships and anatomical context for fine-grained chest X-ray analysis.

title: LieGROG: A Lie algebra approach for calibrating GRAPPA operators
comment: 21 pages, 8 figures, 1 supplementary video (ancillary file). Submitted to Magnetic Resonance in Medicine
summary:
Purpose: In multi-coil acquisitions based on non-Cartesian k-space sampling, image reconstruction using GRAPPA Operator based gridding (GROG) can provide advantages with respect to the non-uniform FFT (NUFFT): It waives both the need for calculating a density compensation function, and for transferring back and forth between Cartesian and non-Cartesian points in iterative algorithms. Non-trivial noise propagation and self-calibration limited to specific trajectories, however, have contributed to GROG being rather sparsely applied so far.
  Theory and Methods: The group structure of the GRAPPA Operator allows estimating its generator as a single joint fit for all k-space dimensions within the associated Lie algebra. Assuming a linear regime, the generator can be fitted using subsequent pairs of sampling points from nearly any arbitrary non-Cartesian read-out. This approach called LieGROG was evaluated against classical GROG calibration and NUFFT/Toeplitz, using simulations with an analytic ground truth and various 2D and 3D MR-scans employing typical non-Cartesian trajectories.
  Results: Throughout all applications, LieGROG proved to provide fast, robust and straightforward calibration of the GRAPPA Operator. It clearly outperformed the classical GROG calibration approaches in terms of noise amplification. LieGROG matched the results of the NUFFT/Toeplitz-based reference MR reconstructions closely, while being 6 to 189 times faster and reducing peak VRAM by 20 to 45% in the 3D experiments.
  Conclusion: LieGROG transforms GROG into a more versatile and stable tool, ultimately aligning non-Cartesian imaging with the standard, FFT-based reconstruction pipelines established for Cartesian scans.

title: GeoDiv KAN Solver for Time Fractional Navier Stokes Equations on Complex Domains to Realistic CFD Reconstruction
summary: Scientific machine learning provides a promising framework for solving complex problems in science and engineering. Notably, physics informed neural networks (PINNs) have shown considerable potential for solving differential equations and modelling engineering systems. Solving time fractional Navier Stokes equations (TFNSEs) on complex domains is challenging due to temporal nonlocality, nonlinear flow dynamics, geometric complexity, and incompressibility constraints. To address these challenges, we propose a geometry gated, divergence-free Gaussian radial basis function Kolmogorov Arnold network (GeoDiv KAN). The proposed architecture uses geometry dependent feature gating and a streamfunction formulation to preserve incompressibility by construction. GeoDiv KAN is evaluated for the time fractional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on square, circular, and star-shaped domains. Numerical experiments show that GeoDiv KAN achieves higher predictive accuracy than PINN, PIKAN, RBF KAN, and DF RBFKAN across the considered benchmark problems. To establish practical relevance, GeoDiv KAN is applied to two data driven CFD cases: unsteady flow past a circular cylinder using the \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5039610}{Zenodo dataset} and turbulent RANS flow through a complex U bend using the \href{https://huggingface.co/datasets/JDecke/ubend-cfd}{U-bend dataset}.

title: CVP-BAA: Efficiently Adapting Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation
comment: Submitted to CVIU, 35 pages, 8 tables, 8 figures. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/WangMei-wm/CVP-BAA}{here}
summary: Various task-specific medical segmentation models have demonstrated strong performance, their heavy reliance on extensive annotations and highly specialized architectures limits their versatility, scalability, and clinical applicability. Recently, adapting vision foundation models, particularly the segment anything model (SAM), has emerged as a promising alternative. However, prevalent parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, such as prompt tuning and adapter tuning, often lack an explicit mechanism to embed local structural priors into the long-range dependency modeling of vision transformers (ViT), rendering them insufficiently sensitive to fine-grained details. To address these limitations, we introduce CVP-BAA, a novel hybrid PEFT method that improves SAM's sensitivity to domain-specific textures and local details, leading to superior boundary delineation. The proposed CVP-BAA adopts two key ideas. First, it introduces a convolutional visual prompting (CVP) strategy that leverages convolutional features as structural priors, prepending them to the key and value projections within the multi-head self-attention layers of strategically selected ViT blocks. Through a dedicated prompt generation-and-injection module, this mechanism effectively bridges local spatial details with global context semantics. Second, a boundary-aware adapter (BAA) is designed as a parallel branch to the feed-forward network within the same selected blocks. By explicitly computing and amplifying high-frequency components, the BAA enhances feature representations along tissue boundaries and fine-grained lesion structures. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks across three imaging modalities demonstrate that CVP-BAA achieves superior segmentation performance, surpassing existing task-specific models and PEFT-based SAM adaptations in both quantitative metrics and qualitative results.

title: AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy
summary: Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy (CLM) enables the visualization of radiotracer uptake in three-dimensional (3D) tumor spheroids but is limited by low photon statistics and spatial blurring caused by positron transport. Here, we present a Monte Carlo (MC)-guided deep learning framework for CLM image restoration. Using TOPAS/Geant4, we developed a physical model of heterogeneous 3D tumor spheroids to simulate positron transport, Cerenkov photon generation and optical propagation. A dataset of 15,360 paired degraded and idealized ground-truth (GT) images was generated from 80 simulated spheroid geometries and used to train a supervised Content-Aware Image Restoration (CARE) network. Compared with the self-supervised Noise2Void (N2V) denoising method, CARE achieved substantially lower reconstruction errors on synthetic validation data, reducing the mean squared error from 0.0492 to 0.0051. Training stability and noise robustness analyses further demonstrated high reproducibility of the restored images. The trained CARE model was subsequently applied to experimental CLM images acquired from 27 U87 tumor spheroids following 18F-FDG uptake. The restored images exhibited more localized intensity distributions and higher local contrast and signal-to-noise ratios compared with raw and N2V-processed images. These findings, aligned with the 3Rs principles of animal experimentation, demonstrate the potential of physics-based supervised restoration to mitigate both noise and positron-induced spatial broadening in CLM.

title: Predicting droplet landing in angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting
summary: Nozzle-free droplet generation eliminates the need for a dispensing orifice, but useful printing also requires control over where droplets are deposited. Here we demonstrate predictable droplet deposition using a nozzle-free, angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting platform. Opposing focused interdigital transducers steer droplets from a pendant parent drop toward a collection substrate, with the ejection angle set by the time-integrated acoustic acceleration imbalance. The overall acceleration ratio identifies the operating window for single-droplet ejection and separates it from no-ejection, satellite-droplet, and multiple-droplet regimes. We then connect ejection angle to landing position through a geometric deposition model referenced to a balanced shot in each experiment. At a 5.2 mm parent-drop-to-substrate spacing, 80 steered shots across twenty experiments show strongly anisotropic relative placement scatter: 0.59 mm in the steering direction and 0.06 mm transverse to it. In tests conducted independently over several days, a model calibrated on six earlier collection dates predicted landing positions on two later dates with a root-mean-square error of 0.71 mm; bootstrap resampling placed the 95% confidence range for this error between 0.41 and 1.01 mm. The results establish a practical framework for predicting relative droplet landing in angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting and identify the limits imposed by steering angle, separation distance, and actuation regime from an orifice-free, clog-free droplet ejection method.

title: GWDM: A Guided Wavelet Diffusion Model for Realistic Histopathology Image Generation
summary: Histopathology images are recognized as a reliable and comprehensive modality for Deep Learning (DL) based diagnosis. However, effectiveness is constrained by limited large-scale annotated datasets, as collecting expert-labeled medical data is costly and time-intensive. Recent advances in generative models, particularly diffusion models, demonstrate strong capabilities in synthesizing medically relevant content for dataset augmentation. Existing generative frameworks treat histopathology patches as generic natural images, failing to enforce biological constraints such as histomorphological structures and heterogeneous staining patterns essential for valid synthesis. We propose a guided wavelet diffusion model (GWDM) framework that captures image details at multiple scales using wavelets and leverages controllable conditioning based on domain-specific histopathological features (e.g., tissue patterns and color variations). We further formulate a histomorphological guidance loss applied to real and generated patches. A loss ramping strategy gradually introduces these constraints during training, ensuring stable optimization and robust modeling of tissue architecture. GWDM was evaluated on three benchmark datasets (BCSS, MoNuSeg, and PAIP2019), consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative methods. Ablation studies confirmed that domain-guided conditioning, perceptual loss, and structural similarity loss each contribute meaningfully to synthesis quality. Downstream nuclei and tissue segmentation experiments further validated the clinical utility of GWDM-generated images, demonstrating consistent performance improvements when synthetic data augments real training sets. This work shows that domain-specific conditioning and dual-loss optimization generate realistic histopathology patches, reducing data scarcity and improving clinical downstream segmentation performance.

title: Direct Production of Ultra-High Radioisotopic Pure $^{64}$Cu from Natural Zinc Metal via D-D Fusion Narrowband Fast Neutron Source Irradiation
summary: Copper-64 radiopharmaceuticals have seen limited clinical deployment primarily due to the high cost of the isotopically enriched $^{64}$Ni metal required for its production. In this work we demonstrate that ultra-high radioisotopic pure $^{64}$Cu can be directly produced in a no-carrier-added-form from natural zinc metal through irradiation with D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron sources. A highly controlled D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron source at the ELI-ALPS Laser Facility was deployed to irradiate encapsulated 99.995\% pure natural zinc for 1 hour. Time-resolved gamma-ray spectroscopy of the irradiated sample over 72 hours was deployed to assess copper radioisotope activity. $^{64}$Cu was the only copper radioisotope detected within the irradiated sample, with a minimum and Minimum Detection Activity (MDA) threshold-corrected $^{64}$Cu radioisotopic purity of 99.62\% and 99.97\% respectively. Our result illustrates that highly controlled D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron sources have the potential to reduce the raw material production costs for $^{64}$Cu radiopharmaceuticals on the order of 2000 times. Cheaper $^{64}$Cu radiopharmaceuticals will increase their use in clinical practice, and, in-turn, increase outcomes for cancer patients receiving radionuclide therapy.

title: Quartz Crystal Microbalance impedance of discrete adsorbates with lubricated contact
summary: We present a thorough theoretical investigation of the shear force exerted on a horizontal plate undergoing fast (MHz range) longitudinal oscillations in presence of a spherical particle suspended in the liquid at close proximity to the plate. This hydrodynamic problem is relevant toward the analysis of frequency response (i.e., complex impedance) of Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) to discrete (particulate) adsorbates. For low areal density of adsorbates, the contributions of individual particles remain additive, rendering the theory applicable towards quantitative interpretation of the experimental measurements. For adsorbates much smaller than the viscous penetration depth, the closed-form analytical expressions for the complex impedance were derived for particles of arbitrary density, assuming a lubricated contact (i.e., non-localized adsorption). The theoretical predictions were shown to be in an excellent agreement with accurate Finite Element numerical computations. The validity of the theoretical approach was confirmed by QCM measurements conducted for polystyrene nanoparticles in a broad range of sizes, from 32 nm to 510 nm, adsorbing onto gold/silica sensor upon varying the oscillation frequency.

title: H-2DGS: Height-Field Gaussian Splatting for Sharp and Deformable Neurosurgical Surface Reconstruction
summary: Neurosurgical navigation commonly presents magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as 2D slices, making it difficult to relate the anatomy in those slices to the cortical surface observed through the surgical microscope. We seek a common 3D visualization that combines a photorealistic reconstruction of the exposed cortex during tumor surgery with whole-brain MRI context and diffusion tractography pathways. This requires the reconstructed cortex to form a clear boundary around the brain anatomy rather than a diffuse volume that obscures internal structures. Conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) can reproduce observed views but, under limited surgical view coverage, may distribute opacity through a thick and geometrically ambiguous band. We introduce height-field 2D Gaussian Splatting (H-2DGS), a three-stage pipeline that concentrates a robust 3DGS reconstruction, fuses its depth into a shared truncated signed distance field (TSDF) surface, and represents that surface with curved, surface-oriented Gaussian primitives. Separate height, color, and opacity bases provide local geometry and appearance, while a neighbor-transition objective coordinates overlapping patches. The explicit surface further supports postoperative alignment: MRI-derived depth deforms the reconstruction, and tracked-color supervision with alternating optimization preserves its appearance. Across five real neurosurgical cases, H-2DGS gives low multi-view depth inconsistency, a compact 7.97MB representation, and interactive rendering at 29--42ms per frame. The resulting sharp, deformable surface integrates clearly with tractography and MRI anatomy, including a postoperative resection cavity.

title: Extracting target-related flow structures using a time-lagged cross-correlation ranking criterion
summary: Structures with large global contributions to a flow field are not necessarily those that are most closely associated with a specified engineering observable. We propose a time-lagged cross-correlation (TCC) ranking criterion to extract target-related dynamical structures from a fixed modal expansion while preserving existing spatial modes and temporal coefficients. The criterion ranks mode groups by the mean squared norm of cross-responses between their flow contributions and the observable over a lag window. It is tested separately using dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). TCC-DMD analysis shows that TCC recovers three low-contribution target structures from a dominant background in a synthetic flow. The reconstruction error for the target subfield is 2.15\%. In the cylinder wake, different force observables select structures associated with the vortex-shedding fundamental, slow drag variations, and the second harmonic. In the cavity case, selected modes connect two main frequency bands of the target observable to distinct spatial amplitude and phase distributions. TCC-POD analysis shows that the criterion minimises the weighted truncation error of the correlation operator among equally sized subsets of the fixed orthogonal basis. A comparison with canonical correlation decomposition further reveals differences between fixed-direction selection and correlation-based basis construction in the spatial structure and retention of flow information. Lag aggregation can improve structure identification when zero-lag association is insufficient. The gains depend on the cross-response distribution and window selection. TCC separates target-related ranking from mode-set construction, enabling comparison of spatial structures associated with different observables within the same modal expansion.

title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
summary: Accurate estimation of diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) is critical for optimising photovoltaic system performance and energy forecasting yet remains challenging in regions lacking comprehensive ground-based instrumentation. Recent advancements using Vision Transformers (ViTs) trained on extensive sky image datasets have shown promise in replacing costly irradiance measurement equipment, but the scarcity of long-term, high-quality sky imagery significantly restricts practical implementation. Addressing this critical gap, this study proposes a novel dual-framework approach designed for data-scarce scenarios. First, calculated atmospheric parameters, including extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings, are integrated to represent sky conditions without utilising any instrumentation. Next, a sequential pipeline initially predicts synthetic global horizontal irradiance (GHI) and uses it as a feature, to refine DHI estimation. Finally, a dual-parallel architecture simultaneously processes raw and overlay-enhanced fisheye sky images. Overlays are generated through unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation to highlight dynamic sky features. Empirical validation is performed using data from the Chilbolton Observatory, chosen for its temperate climate and frequent cloud variability. To simulate data-scarce conditions, models are trained on a single month (e.g., January) and evaluated across a temporally disjoint, full-year test set. Under this setup, the sequential and dual-parallel frameworks achieve RMSE values within 2-3 W/m^2 and 1-6 W/m^2, respectively, of a state-of-the-art ViT trained on the complete dataset. By combining physics-informed modelling with unsupervised segmentation, the proposed method provides a scalable and cost-effective solution for DHI estimation, advancing solar resource assessment in data-constrained environments.

title: A second-order linear decoupled scheme with a relaxed zero-energy variable for Rayleigh-Bénard convection
summary: We construct a second-order, linear, and fully decoupled scheme for Rayleigh--Bénard convection between Navier-slip walls. The nonlinear terms are treated explicitly and multiplied by a scalar with exact value $1$ and no energy contributed to the continuous problem. As a result, each BDF2 step, with a rotational pressure correction, solves only constant-coefficient linear problems. For the time discretization, we prove that, for any time-step, the energy decays when the walls have equal temperatures, under a condition on the thermal weight, and the energy is bounded on finite time intervals when heated from below. Relaxing the scalar towards $1$ preserves both estimates. Energy stability does not control the accuracy of the scalar; the velocity and temperature fields are computed with its unrelaxed value, whose deviation from $1$ scales like $(E/C)(δt/τ)^3$ for kinetic energy $E$, time-scale $τ$ of the flow, and weight $C$ of the scalar equation. In our tests, choosing $C$ comparable to $E$ keeps this deviation small and doubles the largest time-step for which steady rolls are reproduced to a relative difference of $10^{-8}$. With Taylor--Hood elements, we observe second-order convergence in time, recover the critical Rayleigh numbers, and match published Nusselt numbers to within $0.5\%$. A three-dimensional implementation passes corresponding validation tests.

title: GateFormer: Forecast-Space Decomposition for Intra-Hour Solar Irradiance Prediction from Sky Images
summary: Sub-hourly dispatch, balancing, and storage control increasingly depend on forecasts that anticipate rapid variability in solar generation. Accurate sky-image-based irradiance forecasting requires a combination of visual cloud dynamics with recent irradiance state while adapting to different short-term irradiance-change regimes. To address this, we introduce GateFormer, a GHI-conditioned dual-decoder ViT for intra-hour global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting through forecast-space decomposition. GateFormer embeds observed GHI into the visual token stream, allowing interaction with sky-image patch features through self-attention. From this shared representation, a Trajectory Head predicts future GHI sequence, while a Delta Head predicts final-horizon change from the latest observed GHI. The two final-horizon forecasts are adaptively weighted in prediction space, with magnitude- and direction-supervision targeting the remaining error. On the NREL-TSI benchmark, GateFormer attains 125.01 W/m^2 RMSE at +30 min, improving over a state-of-the-art transformer baseline by 9.6% under paired-timestamp evaluation. Across NREL-TSI, Chilbolton, and SIRTA, GateFormer achieves the lowest final-horizon RMSE among the evaluated baselines, with forecast skill of 22.97-28.86% relative to smart persistence. Component ablations show adaptive weighting outperforms both individual decoders and fixed averaging, distinguishing GateFormer from conventional forecast combination, while the supervised correction further reduces RMSE by 1.68 W/m^2 and MAE by 4.86 W/m^2. Ramp-regime diagnostics show larger gains during operationally important positive ramps, reducing RMSE by 26.27 W/m^2. These results identify forecast-space decomposition as an alternative forecasting formulation, with potential relevance to other multimodal short-horizon forecasting tasks and deployment using only sky images and measured GHI.

title: Tandem jets in crossflow: the enclosed-recirculation momentum exchange and the unsteady shear-layer dynamics
summary: Twin tandem jets in crossflow are examined by 40\ kHz time-resolved particle image velocimetry (PIV) over nine spacing--velocity-ratio conditions ($L=2d$--$4d$, $r\approx3$--7; 68 twin cases, 11 single-jet records). The front jet is diluted: its trajectory lies below the single-jet reference, with a near-field segment up to 40\% shorter, and its velocity ratio falls to an effective value $r_{\mathrm{eff}}<r$, while the shielded rear jet rises above the reference. This paper identifies the carrier of that dilution and the unsteady dynamics that sustains it. The rear-jet blockage closes a gap recirculation whose reversed flow puts the two gap-side layers in the counter-current shear-layer configuration, the classical route to enhanced entrainment. The measured Reynolds stress and Prandtl mixing length show that the absolute exchange is nearly independent of the velocity ratio and exceeds the single-jet leeward zone like-for-like by up to $1.5\times$ (zone peak, across conditions) and $2.8\times$ (area-integrated) at $r\approx7$. The gain comes from an enlarged mixing scale rather than from a steeper shear, and the front-jet near-field shortening follows the absolute exchange transport rather than the twin/single enhancement ratio. The turbulent term exceeds the pressure term in eight of the nine conditions, and the flux budget reads the dilution as a limited mass addition plus a momentum loss to the crossflow; the evidence remains observational. The gap-side layers remain convectively unstable---DMD and SPOD find no growing mode within the resolvable band and record length---so the exchange is carried by convecting vortex trains rather than by a self-excited global mode.

title: Bound-Conditioned Latent Inference for Progressive Image Compression
summary: Progressive image compression reconstructs images from prefixes of a single bitstream and therefore involves sequential latent inference under partial observations. Existing trit-plane codecs mainly treat decoded trits as discrete symbols for probability prediction, without fully exploiting their role as interval constraints on the underlying continuous latents. We propose bound-conditioned latent inference (BLI), a framework that reformulates progressive trit-plane coding as sequential latent inference under shrinking interval constraints. At each coding step, the trits decoded so far define lower and upper bounds for each latent element. BLI uses the center and width of these bounds, together with hyperprior information shared by the encoder and decoder, to jointly refine the Gaussian parameters $(μ,σ)$ for entropy modeling and the latent estimate $\hat{y}$ for reconstruction. As additional trits are decoded, the feasible intervals shrink monotonically, yielding tighter constraints for the next inference step and enabling flexible in-plane refinement schedules. Experiments on Kodak, CLIC, and JPEG-AI show that BLI achieves state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance among progressive image codecs, reducing BD-rate by $17.78\%$ over DPICT and by $7.96\%$ over CTC on Kodak, while replacing CTC's plane-specific predictors with a shared model that uses about $5.3\times$ fewer parameters and achieves lower latency than CTC.

title: A novel machine learning framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for turbine wake flow predictions in natural waterways
summary: We developed a machine learning (ML) surrogate trained on instantaneous large eddy simulation (LES) data filtered using proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) to predict mean flow fields in natural rivers with complex geometries. The surrogate enables efficient prediction of mean flow fields downstream of marine hydrokinetic (MHK) turbine arrays at a fraction of the computational cost of high fidelity simulations, facilitating turbine layout optimization in natural waterways where bathymetry, turbulence, and turbine interactions influence the available energy resource. We demonstrate the capabilities of the model at a real world tidal river site under ebb tide conditions. Complex bed bathymetry and planform geometry generate substantial background turbulence that can obscure turbine wake signatures. POD is employed to extract relevant flow structures, improving the ability of the ML model to learn wake dynamics. First, LES is performed at the tidal site to generate training data. POD is then applied to decompose the instantaneous LES fields into spatial modes. Selected modes are used to train a three dimensional convolutional encoder decoder network to predict time averaged velocity fields. This selective filtering reduces the influence of dominant background fluctuations while preserving information relevant to turbine wakes. At equivalent network size and training cost, the POD filtered surrogate reduces the mean squared error by three orders of magnitude compared with the same network trained on unfiltered LES data.

title: QICOM: Open-Source Software for Reproducible Image Quality Evaluation, Blinded Assessment, and Radiomic Comparison
summary: QICOM (Quality Image COMparator) is open-source software for quantitative image comparison, paired radiomics, and blinded assessment. It saves processing settings, image identities, measurements, and response mappings so a comparison can be reopened and recalculated. We evaluate reference agreement, responses to controlled perturbations, and recovery of saved analyses. Synthetic experiments cover 37 quantitative descriptors using independentnumerical references and separate upstream integration comparisons. The QICOM/MIRP backend meets the reference tolerances for all 482 numeric IBSI 1 digital-phantom entries and all 1,622 entries across configurations A-E of the public CT reference case; these comprise 1,804 feature/aggregation comparisons and 300 preprocessing diagnostics. Restricting masked SSIM and HFEN to complete kernel support removes the observed dependence on excluded pixels. In a synthetic filtering example, stronger smoothing increases SSIM while worsening MSE and HFEN relative to milder smoothing and changing GLCM contrast more strongly. Reopened radiomics projects reproduce all 43 feature pairs per comparison, and two blinded deliveries return four correctly mapped scripted responses. These experiments document the calculations and data transfers linking the three workflows.

title: A Priori Estimation of the Non-Linear Compression Potential and Quantification of Autoencoder Non-Linearity in Turbulent Flows
comment: 27 pages, 26 figures, 2 tables. Preprint submitted to Computers & Fluids. Code: https://gitlab.windenergy.dtu.dk/nalpi/how-nonlinear-is-my-flow
summary: Data-driven reduced-order modelling (ROM) of turbulent flows is based on an efficient and physical low-dimensional representation of the flow process. Such a dimension reduction can be achieved using proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) or non-linear autoencoders. Capturing the inherent non-linearities in turbulent flows offers the potential for improved compression rates. This work proposes the local tangent residual (LTR) as an a priori estimate of the potential benefit of non-linear dimension reduction for a given dataset. The LTR is based on the local geometry of the data points, requiring neither prior model training nor the definition of a threshold parameter. For all datasets investigated in this work, namely, two vortex street cases and the turbulent wake flow of a wind turbine, the dominant trends in autoencoder compression performance are reproduced by the proposed LTR. The results are further contextualised through the decoder linearisation error (DLE). The DLE quantifies the non-linearity of the trained decoder by comparing it to a linearised surrogate model, which enables physical interpretability of the non-linearities. Together, a large non-linear compression potential in the turbulent flow, as quantified by the LTR, is corroborated by a large DLE, i.e., a pronounced non-linearity captured in the trained autoencoder. The LTR thus enables practitioners in turbulent flow modelling to determine a priori whether non-linear compression is worthwhile, avoiding the substantial computational cost of autoencoder architecture search and hyperparameter tuning in cases where POD already suffices.

title: Self-Supervised Multibeam Sonar Restoration via Coherent Forward Modeling
summary:
Multibeam imaging sonar produces intensity images degraded by coherent speckle and system-induced blur, while clean reflectivity targets are rarely available. Existing despeckling methods often rely on simplified intensity-domain noise models, synthetic clean targets, or blind-spot self-supervision, and typically do not jointly model deblurring and speckle suppression.
  We propose a physics-consistent self-supervised framework for joint despeckling and deblurring of multibeam imaging sonar. A stochastic coherent image-formation model yields a conditional-mean forward operator that relates latent scene reflectivity to expected intensity through the squared magnitude of the system point spread function. We then use registered multi-frame sonar sequences to train without clean ground truth images, showing that, under an idealized inter-frame conditional-mean condition, the expected paired loss equals the corresponding forward-prediction loss up to a network-independent constant. To stabilize the ill-conditioned inverse problem, we further adapt robust equivariant imaging using stochastic coherent simulation and introduce a paired forward prediction error metric for ground-truth-free evaluation. Experiments on two real multibeam sonar datasets demonstrate a favourable balance between forward-prediction agreement, homogeneous-region speckle suppression, and preservation of visible structural boundaries compared with representative baselines.
